text:
mike_h: Heads up — we’re seeing ~0.9% variance on Feb marketplace invoices. Root cause looks like late-arriving usage events from CloudProviderX (us-east-1). Webhooks were delivered >48h after usage_window_end for a subset of reserved-capacity events. Example: acme-inc got billed baseline instead of burst usage.

accounts_ops: Thanks — can you paste a sample payload or the query you used? need affected-customer list for credits.

mike_h: pasted query i used: ```sql
SELECT customer_id, SUM(tokens) as tokens_late
FROM marketplace_events
WHERE received_at > usage_window_end
  AND timestamp >= '2026-02-01'
  AND timestamp < '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY customer_id;
```
I ran it already — returns 73 customers, ~1.2M tokens total (rough).

sana_ng: Is CPX retry/signature behavior known? any 410/403s in our logs?

mike_h: CPX claims delivered, but our ingestion shows a processing backlog. Logs show transient DB deadlocks around 2026-02-15 03:12 UTC that stalled event processing. No signature failures.

mike_h: Proposal: 1) idempotent backfill/upsert for the late usage events, 2) recompute invoices for affected customers (only Feb window), 3) issue one-time credits where recompute reduces owed amount, 4) publish FAQ + status note.

oliver_s: Agree with approach. Also suggest adding a "delayed" flag on events that arrive after X hours so billing pipeline can treat them differently (avoid double-billing race).

emma_y: I'll draft the PR for the invoice-recompute orchestration and a credit email template for CS. Do we need legal signoff for credits under $50k?

accounts_ops: Finance: credits under $50k total are OK, >$50k per customer needs finance signoff. Send estimate and list by customer.

mike_h: Quick estimate: 1.2M tokens * $0.00004/token = ~$48. That's obviously wrong — sorry brainfart. Recalc in progress.

marketplace_bot: ingestion-monitor: Delay spike detected 2026-02-15 03:00-04:30 UTC — 42k queued events. PagerDuty incident #INC-2026-045 opened.

sana_ng: :thumbsup: Next steps / owners? who will own backfill script and reconciler run?

oliver_s: I'll own the backfill. Plan: branch metering/late-backfill, write idempotent POST script to usage API (batching + retry), run dry-run against staging reconciler, then run prod backfill in controlled batches. ETA: EOD tomorrow for first dry-run.

emma_y: I'll prepare credit template + CS notes and update billing FAQ / status page draft.

accounts_ops: Once oliver posts dry-run diffs + customer list, finance will respond w/ approval within 24h. Make sure to include estimated dollar delta per customer.

mike_h: Oliver — include the SQL that flags duplicates and map events to marketplace_plan_id. Also capture per-event delivered_at and processed_at timestamps so we can show proof for partner/ops.

oliver_s: Pseudocode I'll use for idempotent backfill: ```python
for batch in batches(events):
  for e in batch:
    idempotency_key = f"cpX:{e.event_id}"
    POST /internal/usage 
      {"idempotency_key": idempotency_key, "customer_id": e.customer_id, "tokens": e.tokens, "occurred_at": e.timestamp}
  wait_for_reconciler_sync()
```
I'll also produce a small report: customer -> tokens_added -> invoice_delta.

emma_y: once we have the report i'll prep the email copy + cc CS managers.

mike_h: Thanks — please include a short blurb for marketplace partner (CPX) to ask for root-cause timeline and fix plan. We may need to loop them into any credit questions.

oliver_s: noted. I'll tag CPX partner contact in the postmortem draft.

emma_y: I'll also create a canned CS FAQ: "Why did my usage change after invoice issued?" with steps and timeline.

accounts_ops: Good. Hold off on issuing anything until dry-run + finance signoff.

mike_h: Cool — will follow up with dry-run results here. Thanks all.
